title: Hypotension after Cardiolex exposure
text: We describe three adult patients treated with Cardiolex for hypertension who developed symptomatic hypotension. One patient required hospital admission. The temporal pattern supported a possible adverse drug reaction.

title: Glucorin-associated gastrointestinal events
text: In a synthetic cohort of 80 adults exposed to Glucorin, nausea, diarrhea, and vomiting were the most frequently reported adverse events. No deaths occurred.

title: Severe lactic acidosis signal
text: A patient receiving Glucorin developed severe lactic acidosis and was admitted to intensive care. The report highlights a potentially serious safety signal.

title: Cardiolex adherence study
text: This study evaluated adherence among adults prescribed Cardiolex. Treatment persistence improved after digital reminders; adverse events were not assessed.

title: Hospital formulary redesign
text: A hospital redesigned its formulary interface to reduce medication selection errors. The article did not evaluate Cardiolex, Glucorin, patient adverse reactions, or product exposure.

title: Glucorin in pregnancy simulation
text: A simulated pregnancy registry evaluated Glucorin exposure in 24 patients. One congenital anomaly was reported, but causality and background risk were unclear.

title: Machine learning for PV triage
text: A benchmark compared machine learning methods for adverse event triage using synthetic case narratives. It included no individual product exposure or patient outcome.

title: Rash in Cardiolex users
text: Among 120 adult participants treated with Cardiolex, seven developed a mild rash. The reactions resolved after treatment and none required hospitalization.
